whatItDoes: Authorizes Miller Creek Elementary School District to borrow up to $67 million through bonds for school facilities and equipment, repaid through property taxes. The tax-rate statement estimates an average $27.55 per $100,000 of assessed property value and about $132.5 million in total principal and interest.
yesMeans: Authorize the bonds and property-tax levies to repay them, with facilities-only spending restrictions, independent audits and citizen oversight.
noMeans: Do not authorize these $67 million in bonds or the property-tax levies associated with them.

parts.label: Repayment estimates
parts.what: The estimate is $27.55 per $100,000 of assessed value on average, a highest rate of $30 expected in fiscal years 2027–28 through 2055–56, and collections through 2060–61. Estimated annual debt service is $3.8 million and total principal plus interest is $132.5 million. These are estimates, not binding caps or guaranteed end dates; rates depend on sales, interest rates and assessed values, not market values.

parts.label: Authorized school projects
parts.what: The list covers roofs, bathrooms, plumbing, electrical and heating/cooling systems, classrooms and libraries, technology, accessibility, school security, energy efficiency, playgrounds and outdoor areas. It permits school construction, expansion, replacement, land acquisition and related equipment at existing or future sites.

parts.label: Facilities spending, with related costs
parts.what: Bond money cannot fund ordinary teacher or administrator salaries, school operating expenses, or current routine maintenance and repairs. It may pay costs directly related to listed facilities projects, such as design, permits, construction management, temporary facilities, audits, election and bond-issuance costs, and technology equipment.

parts.label: Project choices and other funding
parts.what: The Board decides project priorities and may change plans or replace a building instead of renovating when appropriate. The money may pay or retire interim financing for listed projects and support joint-use projects with other public entities. No particular project or state matching money is guaranteed; the capital needs exceed this authorization.

parts.label: Audits and public oversight
parts.what: An independent citizens’ committee must be formed within 60 days after results enter Board minutes. Independent financial and performance audits occur annually, proceeds go to a county-held building fund, and an annual report due by January 1 shows collections, spending and project status.

parts.label: Approval and legal borrowing limits
parts.what: At least 55% of votes cast must approve Measure N. Bonds may be issued in multiple series within applicable debt-capacity rules, including any properly granted waiver. County counsel states interest cannot exceed 12% and bonds must mature within 40 years under state law.

parts.label: If part is invalidated
parts.what: If a court invalidates part of the measure, the other provisions remain effective as far as the law allows.

whatItDoes: Authorizes Reed Union School District to borrow up to $115 million through bonds for school facilities and equipment, repaid through property taxes. The tax-rate statement estimates an average $26.63 per $100,000 of assessed value, a highest rate of $30, and about $213 million in total principal and interest.
yesMeans: Authorize the bonds and the property-tax levies to repay them, with facilities-only spending restrictions, independent audits and citizen oversight.
noMeans: Do not authorize these $115 million in bonds or the property-tax levies associated with them.

parts.label: Repayment estimates
parts.what: The estimate is $26.63 per $100,000 of assessed value on average, a highest rate of $30 first expected in 2027–28, and collections through 2060–61. Estimated debt service is $6.2 million a year and $213 million in total principal and interest. These estimates can change and are not binding caps. Taxes are based on assessed value, not market value, and are in addition to taxes for other bond authorizations.

parts.label: School facilities covered
parts.what: The project list includes Reed Elementary, Bel Aire Elementary and Del Mar Middle School. It permits classroom and lab construction or upgrades, roofs and utilities, safety/security and earthquake work, removal of hazardous materials, accessibility and community-use improvements, technology, outdoor/play areas, energy systems and related support facilities and equipment. Land acquisition and new buildings are also allowed.

parts.label: Restrictions and related project costs
parts.what: Proceeds cannot pay ordinary teacher or administrator salaries or other school operating expenses. They may pay facilities work and related design, engineering, permits, legal, audit, temporary-housing and management costs, including district staff work necessary and incidental to bond projects, and retire prior lease or interim financing for listed projects.

parts.label: Board priorities and project changes
parts.what: The Board chooses the order and timing based on needs, readiness and available funding. Some projects may be delayed or not completed. Joint-use projects with other public or nonprofit agencies are allowed. Demolition and reconstruction may replace renovation when the Board finds that more cost-effective.

parts.label: Audits and citizen oversight
parts.what: Independent financial and performance audits occur annually. Bond proceeds have a separate account and statutory reporting. The citizens’ committee must include taxpayer, business and senior-citizen representation; district employees and vendors cannot serve. Spending must stay within the authorized project types.

parts.label: Approval and borrowing limits
parts.what: At least 55% of votes cast must approve Measure O. The tax statement anticipates multiple bond series after a state debt-capacity waiver is received. County counsel states interest cannot exceed 12% and bonds must mature within 40 years under state law.
